title: The claim in neither table
prompt: `claims` has seven claims: one was submitted before its visit, and one is still waiting for the payer, so its `allowed_amount` is empty. This program splits bronze into silver with `filter(passes)` and quarantine with `filter(~passes)`. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

bronze = claims.select("*", F.lit("claims_2026-02-28.csv").alias("_source_file"), F.lit(1).alias("_batch_id"))
bronze.write.format("delta").save("/tmp/clinic/bronze/claims")
bronze = spark.read.format("delta").load("/tmp/clinic/bronze/claims")

passes = (
    (F.col("service_date") <= F.col("submitted_date"))
    & (F.col("allowed_amount") <= F.col("billed_amount"))
    & F.col("claim_status").isin("submitted", "approved", "paid", "denied", "appealed")
)
bronze.filter(passes).write.format("delta").save("/tmp/clinic/silver/claims")
bronze.filter(~passes).write.format("delta").save("/tmp/clinic/quarantine/claims")

silver = spark.read.format("delta").load("/tmp/clinic/silver/claims")
quarantine = spark.read.format("delta").load("/tmp/clinic/quarantine/claims")
print(bronze.count(), silver.count(), quarantine.count())
print(silver.count() + quarantine.count() == bronze.count())
hints: For the claim submitted before its visit, the first comparison is false. What is `false & ...`?
For the waiting claim, `allowed_amount <= billed_amount` compares with NULL. What does that give, and what is `true & NULL`?
`filter` keeps a row only when the condition is true. What is `~` of NULL?
explanation: The claim submitted before its visit makes `passes` false, so `~passes` is true and it goes to quarantine. The waiting claim has no `allowed_amount`, so that comparison is NULL, and `true & NULL & true` is NULL too. `filter` drops a row whose condition is NULL, and `~NULL` is still NULL, so the claim is in neither table: bronze has 7, silver 5 and quarantine 1, and the counts don't add up. A rule that should accept a missing value says so (`F.col("allowed_amount").isNull() | ...`), and the quarantine filter wraps the rule in `F.coalesce(..., F.lit(False))` before negating it, or uses a `when` chain that names the problem. Then every bronze row lands in exactly one table.
